items.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So I called up my best friend, Tommy Flanagan, I said, “I’m moving to New York in two weeks, would you like to go with me?” ... I mean, we were close, you know, so I didn’t have to go into a whole lot of explanation with him.

ctx.x: Did you choose all the musicians on the date?

Oh yeah, well, actually I didn’t know a lot. I chose Tommy and Paul, ‘cause Paul was my protégé, I don’t know if I told you about that. Paul Chambers was a gentleman that I met when I was in Detroit…dances, rather, and I guess like now Hip- Hop is for teenagers, we had some gigs where we played for teenage dancers. And he was at a dance, he was one of the teenagers at this dance that we were playing for. It was me and Tommy, and I don’t who the drummer was, and probably James Richardson, who is Rodney…
We don’t know that much about him.
